tasks.title: Essay: Communication Delay
tasks.instruction: Write an essay summarising and evaluating the key points from both texts in 240–280 words. Use your own words throughout as far as possible, and include your own ideas in your answers.

promptBlocks.label: Text 1
promptBlocks.title: The expectation of instant response
promptBlocks.text: In an era of ubiquitous connectivity, the expectation of an immediate reply has become a default assumption in professional and personal communication. This demand for speed is often framed as a mark of efficiency and responsiveness, yet it exacts a hidden toll. When every message demands an instant answer, the time for reflection evaporates, and responses become reactive rather than considered. The pressure to reply without delay can erode the quality of judgement, as decisions are made without adequate information or deliberation. Moreover, the constant interruption fragments attention, making sustained thought increasingly difficult. The culture of immediacy, far from being a neutral convenience, actively reshapes our cognitive habits and interpersonal expectations. It privileges speed over substance and rewards those who respond quickly rather than those who respond wisely. To treat delayed communication as a failure is to misunderstand the conditions under which careful judgement can flourish.

promptBlocks.label: Text 2
promptBlocks.title: Delay as a safeguard
promptBlocks.text: The assumption that faster communication is always better overlooks the protective function of delay. In many contexts, a lag between message and response serves as a crucial safeguard against impulsive decisions and emotional escalation. Legal and diplomatic protocols, for instance, deliberately build in cooling-off periods precisely because immediate reactions can be damaging. The expectation of instant availability can also create a culture of surveillance, where individuals feel compelled to be perpetually on call, blurring the boundaries between work and rest. In this light, delay is not a failure of responsiveness but a deliberate practice that preserves autonomy and thoughtfulness. Organisations that respect the right to a measured response often report higher-quality decisions and lower levels of burnout among their members. The drive for instant communication, by contrast, can erode trust when people feel pressured to respond before they are ready.

tasks.title: Review: Interactive Work on Silence
tasks.instruction: Write 280–320 words in an appropriate style.
tasks.promptText: An arts and technology magazine is running a series of reviews of interactive works that explore the role of silence in networked life. You decide to submit a review of a recent interactive installation called 'The Quiet Room', which invites participants to enter a soundproofed space and communicate with others only through written notes passed through a slot. In your review, evaluate the interactive form, discuss how effectively the work treats the concept of silence, and assess the effect it has on participants.

tasks.title: Report: Instant Response Expectation
tasks.instruction: Write 280–320 words in an appropriate style.
tasks.promptText: The board risk committee of a financial services firm has asked you to write a report on how the expectation of instant response has affected the organisation. In your report, analyse the behavioural incentives created by this expectation, assess the consequences for decision quality, and recommend policy corrections that could restore more thoughtful communication practices.

tasks.title: Article: Slower Communication and Trust
tasks.instruction: Write 280–320 words in an appropriate style.
tasks.promptText: A public ideas magazine is publishing a series on trust in institutions. The editors have invited readers to submit articles addressing the question: 'Could slower communication produce more trustworthy institutions?' In your article, examine the mechanisms through which a deliberate pace might build trust, consider the costs and objections to slowing down, and discuss the practical limits of such an approach.
